relevance_note: The paper is a case series of four adults with GFAP variants: "Here, we report four adult cases of AOAD".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON from values I typed and checked every span verbatim. Table 2 has patients as columns (headers 'Case 1'..'Case 4'); its cells hold no ' / ' stacked values. Table 1 lists previously described variants with no individual-level patients, so it gives no rows. Scope: 4 probands plus 6 relatives who are affected or tested: Case 2's maternal grandfather, mother and maternal aunt (reportedly similar symptoms; the aunt carries the variant) and father (unaffected, variant not detected); Case 3's mother and maternal aunt (reportedly similar symptoms). Left out: Case 2's two offspring ('not been clinically or genetically confirmed') and Case 3's daughter (asymptomatic, untested). Ages: the text gives age at presentation and disease duration (e.g. '58-year-old ... 5-year history'), not an age at onset, so onset is 'not reported'; presentation age is recorded as age at last evaluation, although the Discussion also reports a six-month follow-up. Palatal myoclonus is excluded for the four cases from 'None of our patients showed palatal myoclonus' (group statement naming the series); I treated palatal myoclonus as the checklist's palatal tremor. Functional evidence is recorded from the named-group statement 'Variant-specific functional studies were not available for the GFAP variants identified in our cases'. Variant type is recorded only for Case 1 ('in-frame deletion'); no type is stated for the others. Inheritance is 'not reported' for all: no parent is stated to carry a variant (Case 2's father tested negative; his mother is not reported as tested). The aunt's variant row gives no zygosity or classification because the paper states those only for the proband. Case 2's transcript is NM_002055.4 while Cases 1 and 4 use NM_002055.5, as printed. Possible inconsistency: Case 3's text says 'mild cognitive impairment' while Table 2 says MoCA '18/30 (significant impairment)'; both are kept in the detail. Case 1's MoCA 20/30 appears only in Table 2. Case 4: 'frequent choking on liquids' is taken as dysphagia, and constipation as bowel dysfunction for the autonomic checklist item; paroxysmal limb weakness is recorded as observed even though examination showed normal muscle strength and tone (episodic versus interictal, not treated as a contradiction). Impaired tandem gait and a positive Romberg sign were not counted as ataxia or cerebellar signs. Seizures stay 'not reported' for Case 4: the episodes lacked convulsive movements and EEG was normal, but the paper does not say she had no seizures. Case 2's checklist autonomic item is excluded from 'Autonomic symptoms were absent.' and normal orthostatic testing. No patient-level ethnicity, consanguinity or vital status is stated.
